original_card.question: Can one uncovered interface implication be formalized with exact caller and certificate bindings?
methods: Formalize a missing boundary lemma identified by the selected review.
Audit a formal theorem-to-certificate binding independently.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State the exact formalized proposition and remaining assumptions; avoid duplicate arithmetic formalizations already present.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one missing statement with quantified hypotheses, actual caller and existing coverage. A compact-switch lemma is a candidate only after its mathematical contract is reviewed. Establish a bounded proof plan before a separately budgeted proof-assistant build; do not rerun large Lean jobs as orientation.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A missing interface proof can reduce the conditional gap even if it does not change kappa.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one formal lemma or one theorem-to-certificate binding.
scope_change_triggers: Formalizing already-covered arithmetic and claiming the full multiplication theorem.

existing_checks.remaining: Exact theorem-to-caller binding and genuinely uncovered interface lemmas.
Uniform algorithmic implications, not another endpoint digit.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: compact-switch formalization proposed as future validation.
existing_checks.remaining: Audit the statement and assumptions before a formal proof campaign.

actual_scope: Prove that a common image line or a common kernel line can never realise the width-two diagonal-pair target at any word length over any field, and that at most two calls never suffice under the #6097 target hypotheses.
scope_change_reason: The explicit field-extension question stored in JoyboyBrian's merged #6097 package replaces the generic interface-lemma task; formal group-algebra obstruction only, no native implementation.
bottleneck_link: A scoped exclusion narrows the open F4/F5/odd-characteristic register search to tuples with at least two image lines and two kernel lines; no primitive saving or complete BIT supplier is claimed.
stop_rule: One written line-exclusion lemma with exact finite corroboration; no claim about the general F4 or odd-characteristic six-call floor.
evidence: PROOF.md and registered verify.py: projector inventories 6/12/20/30, ordered collapse pairs 24/72/160/300, subset collapses and vanishing determinants over F2, F3, F4, F5, two-call diagonal forcing, six-call positive control and mixed-line negative control.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does the six-call diagonal-pair floor hold over F4?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the remaining field scope of the width-two question in #6097.
open_questions.first_step: Run the coefficient-class relaxation of #6097 on the #6609 representatives restricted to tuples with at least two image lines and two kernel lines.
open_questions.blocked_by: The 267,072 five-call F4 representatives have not been searched.

open_questions.question: Does the six-call floor hold over F5 and general odd characteristic?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The even-pairing argument in #6097 has no direct odd-characteristic analogue.
open_questions.first_step: Replace parity pairing by the coefficient-class constraints of the target field.
open_questions.blocked_by: No sound relaxation is known to reject the larger odd-characteristic domains.

open_questions.question: Does the line-exclusion argument extend to rank-one idempotents in M_d(F) for d above two?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would remove the same-image and same-kernel families at larger widths.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat the collapse N_i N_j = N_j and the rank-one factorisation at d above two.
open_questions.blocked_by: The d-fold diagonal target and the paid-call model at larger widths are not specified here.
